statement: The function returns a result q and q equals the number of pairs (l, u) of indices such that 0 <= l <= u < n and there exists an index k with l <= k <= u and nums[k] is even, i.e. divisible by 2. Equivalently, q is the number of nonempty contiguous subarrays nums[l..u] whose product is even.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice satisfies 1 <= n <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: The function returns a result q; it does not fail through overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice satisfies 1 <= n <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result q, 0 <= q <= n*(n+1)/2.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice satisfies 1 <= n <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result q, for every index i with 0 <= i < n and nums[i] even, q >= (i+1)*(n-i).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice satisfies 1 <= n <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result q, q = 0 if and only if every entry nums[i] is odd (not divisible by 2) for all i with 0 <= i < n.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice satisfies 1 <= n <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result q, q = n*(n+1)/2 if and only if every entry nums[i] is even for all i with 0 <= i < n.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice satisfies 1 <= n <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result q, q + O = n*(n+1)/2, where O is the number of pairs (l, u) with 0 <= l <= u < n such that every index k with l <= k <= u has nums[k] odd.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice satisfies 1 <= n <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Let L_1, ..., L_m be the lengths of the maximal intervals [a,b] with 0 <= a <= b < n such that every nums[k] for a <= k <= b is odd and the interval cannot be enlarged without including an even entry; if there are no odd entries then m = 0. Whenever the function returns a result q, q = n*(n+1)/2 - sum_{t=1}^m L_t*(L_t+1)/2.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice satisfies 1 <= n <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Let p_1 < p_2 < ... < p_m be all indices i with 0 <= i < n such that nums[i] is even, and set p_0 = -1. If m = 0 the sum below is empty and equals 0. Whenever the function returns a result q, q = sum_{t=1}^m (p_t - p_{t-1}) * (n - p_t).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice satisfies 1 <= n <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever even_product(nums) returns a result q and even_product(nums') returns a result q', we have q = q'.
preconditions: Let nums and nums' be two slices, each satisfying 1 <= len(nums) = len(nums') = n <= 100000 and 1 <= value <= 100000 for every entry. Suppose that for every i with 0 <= i < n, nums[i] is even if and only if nums'[i] is even.

statement: Whenever even_product(nums) returns a result q and even_product(rev) returns a result q', we have q = q'.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums) and let rev be the slice of length n defined by rev[i] = nums[n-1-i] for 0 <= i < n. Suppose nums, and hence rev, satisfies 1 <= n <= 100000 and 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000 for all i with 0 <= i < n.

statement: Whenever even_product(nums) returns a result q and even_product(nums') returns a result q', we have q <= q'.
preconditions: Let nums and nums' be two slices with len(nums) = len(nums') = n, each satisfying 1 <= n <= 100000 and 1 <= value <= 100000 for every entry. Suppose that for every i with 0 <= i < n, if nums[i] is even then nums'[i] is even; that is, the even positions of nums are a subset of the even positions of nums'.
